text:
anna: Heads-up — after the kselector tweak landed yesterday I'm seeing a 12-18% P99 increase on continuous-batching workloads for a subset of tenants. Repro'd with the replay harness on staging.

mike: Ugh. Is that everywhere or just when KV cache hit-rate is high? Any profile snippets?

anna: It's skewed to tenants with high KV-cache locality. Quick profiler dump attached below (condensed).

anna: ```
GPU util: 72% -> spikes to 95% during bursts
Host CPU: scheduler threads hit 40-60%
Avg batch size: 6 -> suddenly jumps to 12 for ~200ms
KV cache hit: 87%
Kernel chosen: attention_v2_split
Kernel fallback during spike: attention_v1

Noticeable: kernel switch correlates with a spike in scheduling latency and a couple of "no-compatible-kernel" logs.
```

sanjay: That kernel switch + microburst -> means the kernel selector probably flipped based on sequence length distribution window. Did you run apples-to-apples with the same sequence-length sampler?

anna: Yes, same replay trace. Replay config snippet:```
replay:
  max_delay_ms: 8
  batch_size_cap: 32
  continuous_batching: true
  sequence_sampler: fixed_window(0.95, tail_penalty=1.2)
  kselector_policy: heuristic_v2
```

lisa: Can you try forcing kselector_policy: heuristic_v1 and re-run? If the regression disappears that's enough evidence it's selector-related. Also try lowering max_delay_ms to 4 to see if smaller delay prevents batch size jump.

anna: Will run both. Starting run now. @perf-bot can you kick off a 30m replay with the same tenant mix but deterministic seeds? :eyes:

perf-bot: started replay job replay-2143654321-anna (deterministic=true, duration=30m) — logs: https://perf-ci/replays/2143654321

mike: If it is selector oscillation, could be a threshold hysteresis bug. Kernel selection heuristics should include a small dampening window to avoid flip-flopping in microbursts.

tomas: Also check kv cache eviction timing — if a microburst causes evictions, subsequent requests look like cold-starts and kick different kernels. Add a KV cache hit trace to the replay output.

anna: Good catch. I'm enabling kv-hit trace and will attach the diff when run completes. Running heuristic_v1 + max_delay_ms=4 first, then heuristic_v2 with kv tracing.

perf-bot: replay-2143654321-anna finished. summary: P95 +5%, P99 +16% vs baseline. Artefacts uploaded.

anna: Results: heuristic_v1 eliminated the P99 bump (back to baseline). heuristic_v2 with kv tracing shows rapid kernel flips at ~00:12:34 of the replay tied to sequence-length window crossing 128->129 tokens.

sanjay: That sounds like an off-by-one/threshold setting around the 128 boundary. If kernel_v2 switches at >=129 we should make switch hysteresis of +/-8 tokens or require stable window for 200ms.

lisa: Agreed. Also seems batch_size_cap 32 lets microbursts coalesce into big batches; lower cap reduced tail but increased token cost. We need a perf/economics tradeoff doc.

mike: For immediate mitigation: revert kselector change on next canary for dedicated customers and add selector telemetry (window crossing counts) to the runtime logs. Then open a follow-up to add hysteresis.

anna: I'll file the PR to add hysteresis + selector telemetry. Filing issue now and will link bench diffs. Thanks for quick triage. :thumbsup:

anna: Issue: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RINF-9123 — includes replay artifacts and profiler snippets.

lisa: Great. Also schedule an apples-to-apples i/o-normalized run next week so we can quantify token cost vs latency tradeoffs.

mike: 👍 schedule in my calendar.

tomas: Adding a note: if we add hysteresis, include a config flag per-deployment so Dedicated customers can tune tradeoffs.

anna: Noted. Closing the loop here — will post results of hysteresis PR and the cost/latency run in this thread when done.
